Halo stars with unusually high radial velocity (”hypervelocity” stars, or HVS) are thought to
be stars unbound to the Milky Way that originate from the gravitational interaction of stellar
systems with the supermassive black hole at the Galactic center.

values.condition: Speed in the Galactic rest frame reported for HD 271791 (from Heber et al. 2008), cited as an HVS whose proper motion apparently rules out a Galactic center origin

evidence.quote: Nor is the existence of at least one HVS moving at a speed greater than 600 km/s in the Galactic rest frame (HD 271791; Heber et al 2008) whose proper motion apparently rules out a Galactic center origin.

notes: HD 271791: the only individually named star. It is listed as follow-up, not as a new candidate, because the supplied text calls it a previously identified HVS (T:p2-b3) and defines HVS as halo stars thought to be unbound (T:p1-b5); this paper uses its >600 km/s Galactic-rest-frame speed and proper motion to challenge a Galactic-center origin but does not deliver a new present-day bound/unbound verdict for it. The other HVS appear only as unlabeled points in the compilation plots (Fig. 1: I:p3-b0, T:p3-b0; Fig. 2: I:p3-b1, T:p3-b1), and the single 'clearly unbound' HVS mentioned in the Fig. 1 caption (T:p3-b0) is not tied to any identifier. Simulated particles (I:p5-b0, T:p5-b0; I:p5-b1, T:p5-b1) are not observed stars and have no individual identifiers.

HD 271791: The paper gives only a lower limit ("greater than 600 km/s") for HD 271791's Galactic rest-frame speed; no other quantities (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, or radial velocity) are reported for this star in the supplied text. The paper's abstract/introduction also states generally that HVS reach up to ~720 km/s in the Galactic rest frame and mentions stars moving at speeds exceeding ~300 km/s, but these are population-level statements, not values assigned to HD 271791.
